output.brief: The chilled write-off rise is most likely a night-shift handling problem inside the DC, not a Haverlow problem. After the night receiving team was cut from six to four (week 31), night pallets sat at dock for about 3h50m instead of about 44 minutes. The night write-off rate rose from 0.6% to 2.9%, while day-shift rates stayed flat. Haverlow's night write-off rate (3.0%) matches Pellridge (2.8%) and own-label (2.9%), so Haverlow is not singled out. The dock staging lanes are unrefrigerated and ran at 15–17°C overnight. Chambers held temperature and their alarm count was unchanged. I am fairly but not fully sure: the lot-level link between dwell time and spoilage is not yet traced, and the Corriebank credit rise is still unexplained. Next: do not raise the Haverlow chargeback or move volume. Restore night receiving staffing and set a dock-to-chamber limit tracked weekly. Reconcile a sample of Corriebank claims against lots and shifts. Keep the probe in place.
